lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Explicit model: building a ten-minute reset

standardsRefs: Ready for Life v1, Grade 4 Unit 1: Home Care Routines That Last
Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can practice building a ten-minute reset. I will do one step at a time and check one result.
scenario: Building on the four-step five-minute tidy from third grade, the learner now designs their own routine instead of following one fixed sequence.
materials: adult-or-local: one real room that needs a reset

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g4-u01-l02-model-card. Watch one complete example.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g4-u01-l02-guided-card. Do the coached move.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g4-u01-l02-independent-card. Choose one complete route. Follow its steps.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g4-u01-l02-evidence-record. Save one result and one reflection.

prompts.text: Explain one way that choosing your own tasks and order for this ten-minute reset was different from following a fixed routine, and say whether your order was a good choice or whether you would change it next time.

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g4-u01-l02-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g4-u01-l02-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g4-u01-l02-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Planning specificity: Three or four specific tasks are listed and ordered in writing before the timer starts. | Self-evaluation of the plan: The learner accurately reports whether the plan fit in ten minutes and names which task ran long if it didn't. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g4-u01-l02-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner plan and run a ten-minute reset for a second room and compare, in writing, which of their two planned orders worked better and what they would change about the weaker plan.

resources.title: building a ten-minute reset worked model

resources.title: building a ten-minute reset action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal for building a ten-minute reset.
2. Watch the worked move on swk-rfl-g4-u01-l02-model-card.
3. Do one coached move on swk-rfl-g4-u01-l02-guided-card.
4. Complete the chosen route on swk-rfl-g4-u01-l02-independent-card.
5. Save the small record on swk-rfl-g4-u01-l02-evidence-record; use swk-rfl-g4-u01-l02-retry-pair if a step is missed.

resources.title: building a ten-minute reset coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: Building on the four-step five-minute tidy from third grade, the learner now designs their own routine instead of following one fixed sequence.
Coach direction: Look at your chosen room and list everything that would need to happen for it to feel reset.
Learner prompt: List every specific task you notice needs doing in this room right now, for example clearing the table, putting away shoes, or straightening cushions.
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: building a ten-minute reset complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: From your list, choose three or four tasks that realistically fit in ten minutes and decide what order to do them in.
Response 1 (t2-p1): I chose specific tasks from my list rather than trying to do everything.
Response 2 (t2-p2): I wrote my chosen tasks down in the order I planned to do them, before starting the timer.
Response 3 (t2-p3): I thought about which task should go first and why, instead of picking randomly.
Equal-access rule: Use the fictional condition above and complete the same reasoning and evidence without private real-world details.

resources.title: building a ten-minute reset minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.

Reflection: Explain one way that choosing your own tasks and order for this ten-minute reset was different from following a fixed routine, and say whether your order was a good choice or whether you would change it next time.

Success checks: Planning specificity: Three or four specific tasks are listed and ordered in writing before the timer starts. | Self-evaluation of the plan: The learner accurately reports whether the plan fit in ten minutes and names which task ran long if it didn't.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: building a ten-minute reset supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g4-u01-l02-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g4-u01-l02-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional building a ten-minute reset condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Planning specificity: Three or four specific tasks are listed and ordered in writing before the timer starts. | Self-evaluation of the plan: The learner accurately reports whether the plan fit in ten minutes and names which task ran long if it didn't..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g4-u01-l02-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

simulationRoute.completionCondition: Complete the same decision, procedure, evidence, and revision checks as the real-life route. No adult attests that a physical event occurred.

retry.trigger: Start the correction loop when a required step is missing, the reason does not match the condition, a safety or privacy boundary is crossed, or the evidence does not show the stated result.
retry.targetedReteach: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g4-u01-l02-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step.
retry.supportedReattempt: Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g4-u01-l02-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check.
retry.feedback: Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments.
retry.parallelReattempt: Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g4-u01-l02-retry-pair without the coach prompt.
retry.exitCriterion: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Planning specificity: Three or four specific tasks are listed and ordered in writing before the timer starts. | Self-evaluation of the plan: The learner accurately reports whether the plan fit in ten minutes and names which task ran long if it didn't.

guardianInvolvement.role: Optional coach only; no guardian attestation is required.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
